hit.gate_blind_spot_found: THE CONTAINMENT GATE HAS A DEBRIS BLIND SPOT, and this clip is the proof. profile-containment.mjs returned CLEAR (worst TOP 16px, RIGHT 22px, dwell 0) on a clip whose subject pixels demonstrably reach BOTH the top row and the last column. The gate scores the LONGEST CONTIGUOUS border run, so a small detached object crossing an edge — a torn talisman a few px wide — never builds a run long enough to trip any band. Run-length thresholds are the right tool for a limb or a weapon leaving frame and the WRONG tool for confetti/debris. To catch this class you need presence-at-border (any subject pixel in row 0 / column W-1) or a connected-component count, not run length. Recorded rather than fixed: the bbox trajectory (min y0 / max x1 per frame) already exposes it for free and is what caught it here.

The brief kept asking for a visible consequence of an invisible cause, so the model kept inventing a cause. v3 therefore does not just ban the blade — it states positively that the ONLY objects in frame are his own body, fan and sword, which forecloses the whole class rather than the one instance.

v3.the_pattern: THREE VERSIONS, THREE INVENTED ATTACKERS — this is a class, not a run of bad luck. v1 expressed the impact as flying talisman debris (top+right edges). v2, with the talismans locked down, expressed it as a blade from the LEFT. v3, with 'NO blade, NO sword, NO spear, NO arrow, NO projectile, NO weapon ... ever flies in, appears at, or crosses any edge' stated explicitly IN THE BODY, expressed it as a blade from the TOP. BANNING THE OBJECTS BY NAME DOES NOT WORK. The driver is the CAUSAL LANGUAGE: 'HIT REACTION' and 'as an unseen impact lands' instruct the model to depict an impact, and an impact needs a source, so it keeps supplying one at whatever edge is still unguarded. Each ban only moved the entry point.
v3.reroll_fix: v4 ('## hit (stagger — v4, NO CAUSAL LANGUAGE, EMPTY-BACKGROUND LOCK)'), promptLen 3644, fired ~13:2x UTC. NOTHING is ever visible in it — no object, no shape, no blur, no streak, no smear, no shadow' — which closes every edge and every object type at once instead of naming them one at a time. v4.false_alarm_recorded: THE FRONT-TURN FLAG (run 6/97, sym 0.235->0.471) IS MOTION BLUR, NOT ROTATION. f42 is the peak of the recoil snap and the entire upper body is smeared; a blurred silhouette is blobbier and therefore scores HIGHER on selfSym, and the smear also extends the bbox left (min x0 156 @f45), which is what made the mid-frame look like translation. The decisive counter-evidence is that peak aspect stays at 0.67 — the hard tell never fires — and at full size his feet are plainly still on the anchor mark. Same family as the hit v1 false alarm: BOTH front-turn signals read off the bbox, so anything that inflates the silhouette (debris there, motion blur here) corrupts them. Do NOT re-roll for facing or for travel.
v4.what_finally_worked: REMOVING THE CAUSE, NOT THE OBJECTS. v1-v3 all named the impact ('HIT REACTION', 'as an unseen impact lands') and then tried to ban the attacker by enumeration; each ban only moved the entry point (talismans -> left blade -> top blade). v4 deleted every causal word, renamed the beat RECOIL MOTION, described it as pure kinesis ('SNAP backward from the waist in ONE short sharp jolt ... like a man absorbing a shove'), and replaced the blacklist with a POSITIVE whole-frame constraint: 'THE GREEN BACKGROUND AROUND HIM STAYS COMPLETELY EMPTY AND UNBROKEN FOR THE ENTIRE CLIP ... NOTHING is ever visible in it — no object, no shape, no blur, no streak, no smear, no shadow'. That closed every edge and every object type at once. GENERAL RULE for this kit: when a brief names a cause it forbids you to show, the model will keep inventing the cause — describe the EFFECT ONLY.

The hit v4 lesson was applied UP FRONT instead of being rediscovered: the enumerated ban was replaced with the positive whole-frame constraint, worded to still permit HIS OWN dropped fan, sword and hat. victory.qa: REJECT on the START POSE / ANCHOR LOCK. f0 bbox {250,112,595,911} against the kit anchor {239,88,721,911}: IoU vs the kit anchor is 0.6424, where every accepted clip in this kit sits at ~0.99. f0 vs fEND is only 0.7231, so it does not even return to its own opening frame. VIEWED at f0 and f96: at f0 the war-fan is CLOSED, folded to a thin bundle in his hand — the open, spread fan is exactly what extends the anchor bbox out to x1=721, and closed it only reaches 595. By f96 the fan is open and raised and the pose is close to the anchor ({244,114,671,911}), so the clip runs CLOSED -> OPEN: it ends roughly right and starts wrong.
victory.root_cause: THE PROMPT CONTRADICTED ITSELF AND THE ACTION WON. The body said he 'SNAPS the great war-fan fully open with a flourish', which PRESUPPOSES the fan begins CLOSED, while the start-pose lock in the same prompt demanded it already be 'HELD OPEN AND RAISED'. Given two mutually exclusive orders the model obeyed the action verb and started closed. This is an authoring defect, not a model failure — and it is the same mechanism that produced the block_a v2 reject (fan low instead of raised at f0). NEW RULE for this kit, alongside the causal-language rule from hit: AN ACTION VERB THAT PRESUPPOSES A DIFFERENT START STATE SILENTLY OVERRIDES THE START-POSE LOCK. Check every state body for verbs whose precondition contradicts the anchor — open/close, draw/sheathe, raise/lower, plant/step — and rewrite the ACTION, do not just shout the lock louder.
victory.hardening_that_DID_work: The pre-applied v1r locks all held, so they are kept unchanged in v2. CONTAINMENT: CLEAR on all four edges at 0px. EXTRA-OBJECT GATE: 1 blob over the whole clip — NO confetti, petals, sparks or banner, which was the specific risk the positive empty-background wording was added to cover and which the old 'Alone, no opponent' enumeration would not have covered at all. FRONT-TURN: peak aspect 0.59, so he never squared up into a frontal victory pose despite that being the single most likely failure for this state.

The OPENING IS REMOVED FROM THE ACTION ENTIRELY: he now 'RAISES the already-open war-fan up beside his oni face in one slow proud sweep' and lowers it back, with an explicit state lock that the fan 'IS ALREADY FULLY OPEN AND SPREAD IN THE VERY FIRST FRAME AND STAYS FULLY OPEN AND SPREAD WIDE IN EVERY SINGLE FRAME'. Deliberately, the prompt contains NO opening verbs at all — an early draft banned them by name ('NEVER opened, unfurled, snapped open') and that clause was REMOVED before firing, because the hit v1-v3 sequence showed that naming a forbidden action does not prevent it and may evoke it; the positive state lock plus an action that never requires an opening is the whole fix. Build asserted zero occurrences of snapped open / unfurl / SNAPS / flicked open.

ko_suffix_rule: build-prompt.mjs enforces it: `ko` is the ONE off-anchor state, so the shared suffix's weapon lock ('keeps ... in his hands the whole time and never drops or swaps them') and anchor lock ('begins and ends on the EXACT same reference stance') are STRIPPED for ko only. Pasting them verbatim gives the model two mutually exclusive orders — his ko body says the fan and sword SLIP FROM HIS HANDS and he ENDS COLLAPSED. lady-kurotachi.md carries this as a hand-written operator note; ir48's prompt file does NOT, so the rule now lives in the builder instead of depending on whoever fires remembering it.
extra_object_gate: qa-boss/check-extra-objects.mjs — WRITTEN IN RESPONSE TO THIS CLIP. Labels 8-connected components on the keyed silhouette and reports the max simultaneous blobs. Closes the gap that cost hit 4 cycles: profile-containment.mjs scores the longest contiguous BORDER RUN and so misses small debris crossing an edge (it returned CLEAR on hit v1), check-frontturn.mjs reads off the BBOX and is actively CORRUPTED by a detached object (debris pushed hit v1's aspect to 1.06 and tripped the hard tell on a clip in clean side profile), and an intruder that never touches an edge is invisible to both. Calibrated against a known-bad control (hit v3 -> 2 blobs, hit v4 -> 1). DO NOT gate `ko` on it: ko legitimately DROPS both weapons, which correctly reads as extra objects.
